transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because I've been having some trouble staying in my chair. Like during staff meetings at the school, or at dinner. 

I just... keep getting up when everyone else is still seated. I'll get up to refill my coffee, or check a handout, or just walk to the back of the room. It's never really urgent, I just... do it. So, that's what brought me in.
Thinking back, would you say this kind of restlessness and difficulty staying seated has been part of your life since you were a kid, or is this something that's developed more recently, as an adult?

I suppose... it's not really a new thing. Even as a girl, it was there. 

Um, my old report cards used to say I was bright, but that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. My mother actually used to joke that... well, that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. 

So... yes. Since I was a kid.
Besides the restlessness, do you also notice problems like losing track of what you're doing, forgetting important things, or having trouble focusing on tasks like paperwork or reading?

Um... no, I wouldn't say so. I don't really have trouble with my memory or... focusing. I grade my students' essays and handle my lesson plans just fine. It's really just... what I mentioned before. The sitting.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers or comments before someone has finished speaking?

Um... yes, I suppose I do that. 

I... well, in group discussions, I tend to jump in early. Like at my book club, or... during curriculum meetings at school. The response is just... already in my head, and I end up blurting it out before I can really stop myself. So... yes, that happens.
Would you say these behaviors—like getting up frequently or interrupting others—have caused any real problems for you, such as conflicts with colleagues, friends, or family, or issues at work?

I suppose... yes, it has caused some issues. 

Um... people do lose patience with me. At the curriculum meetings, and... the book club I mentioned. I can tell they get frustrated when I interrupt or can't sit still. It... it just makes me feel embarrassed, honestly. I go to those things wanting to connect with people, and I end up leaving feeling... well, embarrassed. So, yes. It affects things.
Do you notice this same restlessness and urge to interrupt happening at home as well, like when you're with family or relaxing alone, or is it mainly in meetings and social settings?

Um... yes. It happens at home, too. 

Like... during quiet evenings with my husband. I just have a hard time sitting quietly with a movie, or a book. Before I know it, I'm... making comments out loud, or I'm up rustling around in the kitchen. Or I'll just suggest we do something else entirely. So... yes, it's not just at work or the book club.
